request.summary: Create a Team Presence Board signage widget that shows live Microsoft Teams availability for configured team members from an existing Wallboard presence datasource, with adaptive dense, quadrant, compact, and hero door-card layouts selected by the number of people displayed.
request.audience: Employees and visitors glancing at lobby walls, department screens, small team zones, and office door displays.
request.primaryGoal: Answer at a glance who is available, busy, away, or offline right now, including the door-card question: can I interrupt this person?

assumptions: The presence datasource already exists on the customer server and is bound by a human in the Wallboard editor at deployment time; the app never fetches URLs or embeds datasource IDs.
The nested users array in the presence payload cannot be flattened to TABLE without losing structure, so the app binds the existing datasource shape directly and normalizes it at one boundary.
Presence status colors remain constant across Dark, Light, and Custom themes because they are semantic Teams availability colors.
Status-change durations are tracked locally by diffing datasource updates; until a change is observed the duration is unknown and only the status label is shown.
All bundled roster data, names, emails, IDs, and photos are synthetic; photos in fixtures are embedded data-URI portraits so previews work offline.
The Wallboard logo is intentionally omitted because screens carry branding elsewhere.
When a zone holds more people than physically fit its measured area, the zone shows the cards that fit plus a +N overflow chip; the zone count always reports the true total.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: One app serves full-company lobby walls, department screens, small team zones, and portrait door-card displays of unknown zone sizes, so the root must fill any surface without viewport assumptions.

surfaces.purpose: Quadrant board with four presence zones for department and team screens.
Wide band placement keeping zones side by side with compact cards.
Portrait wall or door-side placement with stacked presence zones.
Compact square zone preserving zone identity with smaller cards.

ownership.rationale: The count-driven layout modes, availability normalization, and status-change motion are the validated product core and stay code-owned.
Operators name the scope shown under the board title per placement.
Operators choose exactly who appears on each placed instance.
Header and ticker are toggleable per physical scenario.
Coordinated Dark and Light presets resolve the palette; Custom exposes manual swatches; motion is optional.
The directory and Teams presence feed are pushed by the displayer from the bound existing datasource.
Since-timestamps and the last observed change are derived locally per instance by diffing datasource updates.

views.purpose: Dense quadrant wall for 21 or more people on full-company lobby screens.
Four presence zones (Available, Busy, Away, Offline) for 4 to 20 people.
Full-height per-person panels for 2 to 3 people.
Single huge door-card avatar answering whether one person can be interrupted.
Designed empty state when no valid people match the configuration.

session.expectation: The passive board continuously reflects the latest pushed presence data.

rendering.rationale: Zones, cards, and the hero composition reflow between landscape, portrait, wide-low, and compact square placements.

motion.rationale: The stakeholder-endorsed FLIP-style glide moves a card between zones on status change with a landing pulse; Subtle crossfades in place; Off and prefers-reduced-motion update instantly while every timer cleans up.

media.fallback: Render a colored initials disc from a fixed 12-hue palette assigned by roster index; broken photo URLs fall back the same way.
media.rationale: Profile photos arrive as URL fields on the bound presence records and use the platform cache; previews embed synthetic data-URI portraits.

branding.provenance: Wallboard brand aesthetic from the stakeholder-approved prototype: torch red accent, square corners, charcoal signage palette; no logo is embedded.
branding.fallback: Coordinated Dark preset palette with torch red accent.

settings.purpose: Scope subtitle shown after the board title in the header.
Comma or newline separated email prefixes or full addresses selecting exactly who is shown; empty shows everyone passing the photo rule.
When the member filter is empty, only people with a profile photo are shown to exclude service accounts.
Toggles the header bar with title, scope, clock, and live pill.
Toggles the footer ticker showing the last observed status change.
When off, offline people are hidden and the board becomes a three-zone layout.
Selects the coordinated Dark, Light, or Custom color scheme.
Custom header and footer well color.
Custom accent color for the live pill, header rule, and highlights.
Selects Off, Subtle, or Expressive status-change motion.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize the scope tail while the fixed board title stays complete.
dynamicText.rationale: The configurable scope must never displace the clock or live pill.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize long names on one line; the status badge, ring, and zone identity are never lost.
dynamicText.rationale: Names vary widely; identity is preserved by avatar, ring color, and badge even when the tail is ellipsized.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize long names on one line at the compact scale; ring and badge keep identity readable.
dynamicText.rationale: Compact panels carry one large name that must stay on a single line.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize long names on one line at the door-card scale; ring and badge keep identity readable.
dynamicText.rationale: The door card carries one huge name that must stay on a single line.

dynamicText.fallback: The humanized status stays on one line so card cells keep a deterministic height for zone capacity; the rare overlong tail ellipsizes.
dynamicText.rationale: Grid cards need stable geometry so each zone can cap itself at the cards that fit and never clip content.

dynamicText.fallback: Uppercase status wraps to a bounded second line before the separate duration line is omitted.
dynamicText.rationale: The compact status is a large uppercase statement in the status color.

dynamicText.fallback: Uppercase status wraps to a bounded second line before the separate duration line is omitted.
dynamicText.rationale: The hero status is a large uppercase statement in the status color.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize the tail of the last-change line inside the fixed-height ticker well.
dynamicText.rationale: The ticker is one quiet line and must never wrap or resize the board.

states.expectation: Twenty-five or more people render the dense quadrant wall with smaller cards and every zone scannable.
Three people render full-height compact panels with status-tinted radial glows and uppercase status labels.
A single person renders the huge door-card avatar with ring, badge, glow, and uppercase status.
The coordinated Light preset resolves the full palette while presence colors and contrast hold.
An empty or unmatched roster renders the designed empty state, never a blank widget.
A payload without a valid users array renders the designed data-problem state without crashing.
All-offline rosters show grayscale dimmed avatars and the non-offline zones show faint empty-zone labels.
Missing and broken photo URLs fall back to colored initials discs from the fixed palette.
Very long names, scope, and status labels ellipsize or wrap without displacing card geometry.
With the offline zone hidden, offline people disappear and the remaining three zones fill the board sensibly.
With header and ticker off, the zones fill the full surface cleanly.
A pushed datasource update changes a person's zone, stamps the since time, and updates the ticker without rebuilding the app.

behaviors.expectation: Layout mode follows visible people count: 1 hero, 2-3 compact, 4-20 quadrant, 21+ dense quadrant.
Availability values map to the four presence groups, activity-preferring humanized labels, and duplicate or service-account records are skipped.

A status change glides the card between zones with a landing pulse when motion is Expressive, crossfades in place when Subtle, updates instantly when Off, and all animations and timers clean up on destroy.
Observed status durations format as just now, minutes, then hours and refresh on an instance-local tick that is destroyed on cleanup.
The member filter matches email prefixes or full addresses case-insensitively; empty filter applies the photo rule.
Pushed datasource updates re-render presence in place and update the ticker.
Each zone renders only the cards that fit its measured area and summarizes the remainder as a +N chip instead of clipping content.
Every presence card states availability in words as well as by the coloured ring, and that text stays legible against the card.

visualDirection.summary: Recreate the approved dark charcoal Team Presence prototype: square-cornered zones, torch red accents, circular status-ringed avatars, and count-adaptive quadrant, compact, and hero compositions.
references: Stakeholder-approved single-file HTML prototype and its hosted demo, including the door-card variant.
Wallboard brand rules: torch red accent, square corners everywhere except avatars, badges, and dots.
signatureChoices: Count-adaptive composition: dense quadrant wall, 2x2 quadrant zones, full-height compact panels, and a single hero door-card from one codebase.
Circular avatars with 3px status-colored rings and corner glyph badges as the primary scan target against square-cornered charcoal zones.
FLIP-style card glide between zones with a status-colored landing pulse as the live signature.
Header with pulsing LIVE pill and 3px torch red rule; footer ticker reporting the last observed status change.
avoid: Rounded-corner card dashboards or generic dark operations templates with top accent rails.
Embedding the Wallboard logo inside the app surface.
Copying the prototype stylesheet wholesale; clamp() and flex gap are forbidden by the legacy pipeline.

visualReview.intent: The board should read as the same product as the approved prototype at every count tier: instantly scannable presence with brand-true charcoal and torch red styling.
focus: Compare each layout tier against the prototype: zone headers with swatch and count, avatar ring and badge geometry, compact glow, and hero scale.
Verify long names and status lines never displace card geometry and descenders keep ink clearance in fitted and ellipsized lines.
Verify Light preset contrast on zone headers, muted text, and the ticker; presence colors must stay recognizably constant.
Verify offline treatment: grayscale dimmed avatars must remain identifiable and empty zones show faint labels rather than voids.
